chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad and Ahmad from Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi from Marwan ibn Muslim from Abdullah ibn Bukayr and Ubayd and a group of our companions, they said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

"There is no zakat in the wealth that is fluctuating (uncertain)." His son Ismail said to him, "I am your ransom, father, you have consumed the poor of your companions." He said, "O my son, it is a right that Allah intended to take out, so it came out."

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ ابْنُهُ: His son Ismail (referring to Ismail ibn Ali)
key_terms.الْمَالِ الْمُضْطَرَبِ: Fluctuating or uncertain wealth (where the exact amount or value is not fixed)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zakat for fluctuating or uncertain wealth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'mutadharib' wealth—assets whose value or quantity is fluctuating and uncertain—does not incur zakat, addressing the concern of his son Ismail that this might deprive the poor. The Imam’s response, 'It is a right Allah willed to be removed,' underscores the divine wisdom behind specific fiscal exemptions, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that zakat obligations are strictly defined by divine decree rather than mere economic utility. This distinction highlights the precision in Shia fiqh regarding the assessment of assets, ensuring that uncertainty does not lead to undue burden or arbitrary collection.
